note:
1911 household schedules supplied by A. Hagues, filling the second half of the gaps the census-gap report found - the streets the record holds in 1891 and again in 1921 but not in 1901 or 1911.

**These are the householder's own schedules, not the enumerator's book.** The hand is the head of the household's, the signature at the foot is his, and the 1911 return asks a woman three questions no earlier census did: how long she has been married, how many children she has borne, and how many are still living. Those answers are kept here because nothing else in the record can supply them.

**Not named people_*.json on purpose**, so the importer never reads it. A reading I am unsure of carries [?].
source: 1911 census household schedules - transcribed by Claude from images supplied by A. Hagues

marriage.note: Married about 1878. The four are Harold (1879), Oswald (1882), Dorothea (1884) and Ursula (1891), and in 1911 all four were alive.

people.name: John Kenneth Varvill
people.note: Entered first as NEPHEW, struck through and altered to Visitor in the same hand.

households.note: Fills the 1911 half of the gap at 9 Newcastle Drive. The record holds John (#2128), Jessie (#2129) and Ursula in 1891 and again in 1921, so this is the middle of a run of at least thirty years in one house - the longest single tenure the gap report turned up on that street.

**THE GAP REPORT READ THIS AS TWO CHANGES OF FAMILY, AND IT IS ONE MAN MOVING HOUSE.** William Thomas Cartwright is at **1 Newcastle Drive** in 1891 and at **7** in 1901, 1911 and 1921. The report showed 1 Newcastle Drive as Cartwright-to-Copeland and 7 as Birkin-to-Cartwright, because it compares each house with itself and cannot see a household walk down its own street. His daughter Margaret Helen (#2153) carries both ends - 1891 at number 1, 1921 at number 7.

Mary J. Cartwright, his wife, is alive in 1901 and he is a widower here, so she died between the two returns. Vincent Henry (#1781, born 1883) is already in the record, at 2 Park Ravine by 1921.

people.name: Charlotte Loder
people.note: "Coachman" was written in her occupation column and struck out - her husband's trade carried down a line by mistake.

people.name: Stanley Loder
people.note: Charlotte gives three children in twenty-six years and she is 54, so an infant of eighteen months is very unlikely to be hers. A grandson, with the relationship column left blank.

households.note:
**SETTLED BY THE SCHEDULE COVER: *Back of 5 Newcastle Drive, The Park, Nottingham*.** The enumerator first wrote *Huntingdon Drive, The Park*, struck it through, and wrote the back of 5 underneath. So this is the coach house or stable flat behind **5 Newcastle Drive (#210)**, and A. Hagues had it right.

**My reasoning against it was worthless.** I argued from the schedule numbers - 14 at number 7, 18 at number 9, so 17 must fall between them - and an enumerator numbering back premises does not walk in a straight line. An address written on the paper beats an inference from the order of the paper every time.

**And the big house ties the two together.** 5 Newcastle Drive on the same night is Henry Gee's, and one of his four servants is **Fanny Charlotte Loder**, housemaid, 24, born Nottingham. Charles and Charlotte Loder are at the back with a son of 16. Fanny Charlotte is almost certainly their daughter: the coachman drives for the house, his wife keeps the coach house, and his daughter is in service in the front of the same property.

**Charlotte reports three children born alive and three still living.** Charles Wood, 16, and Fanny Charlotte, 24, are two of them. The third is elsewhere. Stanley, eighteen months, is not one of the three, so he is a generation down - whose is not on the paper.

people.name: Fanny Charlotte Loder
people.note: Almost certainly the daughter of Charles and Charlotte Loder at the back of this same house - schedule 17.

households.note:
Closes the 1911 half of the gap at 5 Newcastle Drive. The record holds **Thomas Hill**, hosiery manufacturer, there in 1891 and again in 1901 at 78 and widowed - and **Henry Gee** there in 1921. This puts Gee in the house by 1911, so the handover happened in that decade, and one hosiery manufacturer followed another into it.

Clara married about 1871 and bore two children, both living in 1911. Neither is in the house.

The cover gives the district numbers for the whole round: registration district 430, sub-district 1, **enumeration district 11** - which is the district to ask for if the rest of this 1911 round is wanted.

people.name: Mary Elizabeth Patterson
people.note: The record holds her as **Mary ELY Patterson**. This return writes it out as Elizabeth, and A. Hagues confirms it. Ely is a misreading of an abbreviated Elizth.

people.name: Emma Jarvis
people.note: The index reads the birthplace as "Bowns"; the record has Bourne from both 1891 and 1901, so Bourne it is.

people.name: Dora Muffel
people.note: The index reads "Manla Cambs". Manea is a Cambridgeshire village and the likeliest reading, but it is a guess at one letter and is marked as one.

households.note:
Closes the 1911 half of the gap at 1 Park Terrace. The record holds Mary Patterson there in 1891 and 1901 and a different family, the Cockburns, by 1921 - so this is the last census of her tenancy, at 82 and still keeping two servants.

**Emma Jarvis has been with her at least twenty years.** She is a servant in this house in 1891 at 31, in 1901 at 46 and here in 1911 at 51 - one woman across three returns, with the ages drifting as census ages do.

**And she is in the record twice because of that drift.** #3585 carries her 1891 row at born 1860; #4757 was created by the 1901 gap-round import at born 1855, because the page gave her age as 46. Five years apart, so neither the duplicates page nor variant_duplicates.py can see them - both test born years within two. This return gives 51, which agrees with #3585, so #3585 is the one to keep.

people.name: Kate Reid
people.note: **Kate Elizabeth Reid (#1789).** The record has her at 6 Park Terrace in 1901 as the sister-in-law of William H. Foster - I transcribed that page as *Kate E. Reis* - and back at 2 Park Terrace as head in 1921. Married twenty years and widowed by 1911, with no children born to the marriage.

people.name: Frances Mary Wing
people.note: **Almost certainly Frances May KING (#1790) of the 1921 return** - same house, same birth year, same birthplace, and a second Head beside Kate Reid there in 1921 just as she is Joint Tenant here. King for Wing and May for Mary: two single-letter misreadings in one name. She is also very likely the Frances Wing, 36, who is Henry Wing's daughter at 12 Park Terrace on the 1901 round.

households.note:
Closes the 1911 half of the gap at 2 Park Terrace, and it is not a family at all: two women of independent means keeping house together, one a widow and one a spinster, entered as **Head and Joint Tenant**. The record has the same pair there in 1921, where the transcription made them two Heads.

**"Joint Tenant" is a relationship the record has nowhere else.** It is worth keeping as the page wrote it rather than flattening it to lodger or boarder, because it says something the other words do not: neither woman was the other's dependant.

**And it settles the Wellington question.** Kate Reid was genuinely born at Wellington, New Zealand, so the record's two rows under that place are right. The record also holds one *Wellington, Somerset*, which is a different place and a different person.

people.name: Herbert Bradley
people.note: **#1796.** This is the fourth census of him the record now holds: a boarder at 10 Park Terrace in 1891, head of number 3 in 1901, here in 1911, still there in 1921. He was the anchor picked for searching this street and he has turned out to span it.

people.name: Mary Saxby
people.note: **Recorded as 45 in 1901 AND 45 here, ten years apart**, and the record holds two Mary Saxbys at this house - #4760 born 1856 from the 1901 round and #1797 Mary E Saxby born 1861 from 1921. Three birth years and three birthplaces (Somercotes, Derby, Southwell) for one servant in one house. Almost certainly one woman; not bound to either number here, because which is the keeper is not something this page can settle.

households.note: Closes the 1911 half of the gap at 3 Park Terrace. Eight rooms, three people, and the householder's own signature at the foot.

A household entirely new to the record, and entirely Cornish. **Four of the five Thomases were born at St Michael's Mount** - a tidal island of a few dozen souls - and their widowed mother a little inland. A dentist of 35 keeping house with his mother and three unmarried sisters, three hundred miles from where all of them were born.

1901 held Herbert Lancashire, hosiery manufacturer, so the house changed hands entirely in the decade.

people.name: Annie May
people.note: Entered as Single with "Widow" struck through - the householder changed his mind about her.

households.note: **9 Park Terrace is usually empty, and this is the only household the record will hold for it.** It was returned uninhabited in 1901, holds two people in 1891 and nobody at all in 1921. Here a newly married couple - the marriage under a year old and no children - with a cook and a housemaid.

people.name: John Henry Runge
people.occupation: Secretary in a limited liability company, lace
people.note: **Born in Germany and naturalised in 1875**, which the schedule states outright. The record has him as a naturalised British subject from the 1891 return but not the year.

households.note:
**This is the house he moved to, and it closes the Park Valley question.** The record holds John Henry Runge at 17 Park Valley in 1891 and at 10 Park Terrace in 1921; the gap report could only say a Runge had gone from one and arrived at the other. He is here in 1911, so the move happened between 1901 and 1911 - and 17 Park Valley already held William Ranson, physician, by 1901.

**And the 1911 questions say something no other return could.** Married forty years, **one child born alive, none still living, one died**. A marriage of forty years and a single child who did not survive - a fact the record could not have held before, because only the 1911 census asked.

**A woman heads this house and she is a head mistress** - the only one the record holds. She keeps a housekeeper and takes a boarder, a young assistant dental surgeon from Cheshire. Three people, all single, none related to each other.

Her surname is read here as Nicolls and her employer as the Midland Institute; both are uncertain in the hand. 1901 held Richard Beaumont, solicitor, so the house turned over entirely.

people.name: Charles Edward Townroe
people.note: The hand is hard and an index may read the surname as Tannoc. It is Townroe: the same forenames, the same rare middle name in his wife, the same trade and the same town.

people.name: Mary Dakeyne Townroe
people.note: **The record spells her Daykene**, from the 1891 return. Her husband writes it **Dakeyne** here in his own hand, which is the better authority.

households.note:
**THE TOWNROES, AND THIS IS WHERE THEY WENT.** The record holds Charles Edward and Mary at **2 Lenton Road** in 1891, and A. Hagues's reading of the 1901 round put them still there under the hand's *Tomnroe*. Here they are at 12 Park Terrace in 1911 - the same couple, the bank clerk and his wife, one street over.

**And the marriage questions account for the children.** Married twenty-seven years, so about 1884: **three born alive, two still living, one died**. The record holds Bernard Stephen (1885) and Sybil Mary (1889) from 1891 and Geoffrey C. (1895) from 1901 - three children, and one of them did not live.

people.name: Frederic Dunnill
people.occupation: Organist and teacher of music | Own account

households.note:
**An organist and teacher of music**, working on his own account - the second musical household the record has found on the estate, after the Horners, father and son, both professors of music at Oakleigh on Hamilton Drive in 1901.

Newly married, under a year, and no children. 1901 held Richard Beaumont, solicitor, with one housekeeper.

people.name: Tinsley Lindley
people.note: **#1819.** The record holds him at this house in 1901 and 1921 and as **Tinster Lindey** in the 1921 transcription. He signs this schedule himself: **Tinsley Lindley**.

people.name: Constance A. Lindley
people.note: **The record holds her twice and neither is right.** #1820 *Constance Agnes Lindey* from 1921 has the forename but not the surname; #4785 *Constance Lindley* from the 1901 round has the surname but not the forename. Her age here agrees with #1820.

households.note:
**Tinsley Lindley in his own hand.** He is in the record at this house across three censuses and is not marked as a notable resident, which on the face of the record is reasonable - a barrister of 45. He was also an England footballer, and worth looking into before the record settles on calling him a lawyer.

**And the marriage answers close his family.** Married fifteen years, so about 1896: **one child born alive, one still living**. That is Victoria, four years old on the 1901 round and the only child they ever had.

A young household entirely new to the record: a box manufacturer of 29, his wife, a baby of nine months, and two servants - a cook and a nurse for the one child. Married two years, one child born and living.

**Margaret Dunn was born at Pittenweem in Fife** and is marked *Resident* rather than visitor, so she had come south for the work. 1901 held Joseph Youngman, a bank manager of 50, with his sister.

people.name: Fredk Harold Maden Eberlin
people.note: New to the record. It holds his brother **Albert Edgar (#1829), born 1895**, from the 1921 return - and the marriage answers here give two children born and two living, so the pair of them are the whole family.

households.note:
**The two servants are sisters.** Louisa and Nellie Wharmby, 23 and 18, both born at Underwood - a mining village north-west of the city - in service together in the same house. Neither is in the record.

The Eberlins are held at this house from the 1921 return; this puts them there ten years earlier. 1901 held William F. Bromley, stockbroker.

people.name: Elizabeth Helen Brewster
people.note: **British subject by parentage**, which the schedule states. The record already has her birthplace as Ostend from the 1891 return; the 1901 round I read gives only "Belgium".

people.name: Mary Allsebrook
people.note: **Still with her after ten years.** She is a cook in this house in 1901 at 25 and a lady's maid here at 38 - thirteen years of drift in ten, which is why the duplicate checks cannot pair the two rows.

households.note:
**John T. Brewster died between 1901 and 1911.** The record holds him at this house as a solicitor of 72 in 1901; here his widow keeps it alone at 76, with three servants and no family. Married twenty-nine years and **no children born to the marriage at all**, which the 1911 return states and nothing else could.

Four women in eleven rooms, one of them Belgian-born, and not one of them related to another.
